@@ -66,13 +66,27 @@ To enable these features, the following component properties combinations must b
-|||negotiationType|NONE or TLS|Optional. The TLS/SSL not checking for this type, but strongly recommended.
+|||negotiationType|PLAINTEXT or TLS|Optional, but TLS is strongly recommended: with PLAINTEXT the token is sent in clear text, and whoever reads it can make calls with it until it expires
+|||jwtTokenLifetime|1 hour (default)|Optional. On a producer: how long a token is valid (the exp claim). 0 sends a token without expiry
+|||jwtMaxTokenAge||Optional. On a consumer: the maximum age of a token by its iat claim. Not checked by default
+With `authenticationType=JWT`, the producer sends a token with the `iat` (issued at) and `exp` (expires at) claims,
+which is valid for `jwtTokenLifetime` (1 hour by default). The producer creates a new token when less than a tenth of
+the lifetime, at most one minute, is left of the current one. With `jwtTokenLifetime=0` the producer sends a token
+without `iat` and `exp`, as before Camel 4.24, which is valid until `jwtSecret` changes.
+The consumer rejects a token whose `exp` claim has passed, and a token whose `iat` claim is in the future. A clock
+difference of up to one minute between the hosts is accepted. A token without `exp`, such as one from another client,
+is accepted until `jwtSecret` changes, unless `jwtMaxTokenAge` is set: then the consumer also rejects a token that is
+older than `jwtMaxTokenAge` by its `iat` claim, or that has no `iat` claim.
